access_token.description: Access token used to interact with Ori Global Cloud. Can be provided via OGC_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable.

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the Application.

fs_group.description: Supplemental group that applies to all containers in a pod.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Application.

last_updated.description: The timestamp of the last change to this entity and any sub-entities.

max_instances.description: The maximum number of cross-cluster instances (Default = 1) of this application to deploy. 0 value has special meaning as noted in the Multiplicity section below.

min_instances.description: The minimum number of cross-cluster instances of this application to deploy.

min_ready_seconds.description: Setting for minReadySeconds on all Kubernetes Deployments which are generated by this Application.

name.description: The user-supplied RFC 1123-compliant name of the Application.

package_id.description: The id of the parent Package of the Application.

progress_deadline_seconds.description: Setting for progressDeadlineSeconds on all Kubernetes Deployments which are generated by this Application.

reject_privileged_clusters.description: If true the planning algorithm will refuse to place the application on a Cluster for which permitPrivilegedContainers is true. Prevents owned Clusters setting privilegedAccess to true.

replicas.description: The number of replicas of the Application to be deployed to a single Cluster.

requires_redeploy.description: Set to true if the Application needs the entire owning Package to be redeployed when the Application is restarted for stability reasons.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Selector.

key.description: The key that is used to match the key property of a Label.

operator.description: The SelectorOp used as part of the label matching operation. Can be one of: Exists, NotExists, Equals, NotEquals, In, NotIn, MinOf, MaxOf. Defaults to In.

values.description: The values to be used during deployment planning. If operator is Exists, NotExists, MinOf or MaxOf this should be empty.

block.description: An Application may have zero or more Selectors associated with it. These Selectors are used during deployment planning to select which clusters the application can run on.
Applications are groups of one or more containers, with shared resources such as networking and storage, that can be deployed and replicated across clusters or in a single cluster.

agent_version.description: The version of the agent installed on the Cluster.

description.description: The user-supplied description for the Cluster.

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the Cluster.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Cluster.

labels.description: Labels used by the deployment planning algorithm to place workloads in the appropriate clusters.

name.description: The user-supplied RFC 1123-compliant name of the Cluster.

organisation_id.description: The id of the parent Organisation.

permit_privileged_containers.description: Specified whether the Cluster is allowed to run containers which require privileged access.

status.description: The current status of the Cluster.

client_certificate.description: PEM-encoded client certificate for TLS authentication.

client_key.description: PEM-encoded client certificate key for TLS authentication.

cluster_ca_certificate.description: PEM-encoded root certificates bundle for TLS authentication.

config_context.description: Context to choose from the config file.

config_context_auth_info.description: Authentication info context of the kube config (name of the kubeconfig user, --user flag in kubectl).

config_context_cluster.description: Cluster context of the kube config (name of the kubeconfig cluster, --cluster flag in kubectl).

config_path.description: Path to the cluster kube config

host.description: The hostname (in form of URI) of Kubernetes master.

insecure.description: Whether server should be accessed without verifying the TLS certificate.

password.description: The password to use for HTTP basic authentication when accessing the Kubernetes master endpoint.

proxy_url.description: URL to the proxy to be used for all API requests

tls_server_name.description: Server name passed to the server for SNI and is used in the client to check server certificates against.

token.description: Token to authenticate an service account

username.description: The username to use for HTTP basic authentication when accessing the Kubernetes master endpoint.

block.description: Kubernetes configuration of the underlying cluster.
A cluster where applications created in OGC can be deployed to.

application_id.description: The id of the parent Application of the Container.

args.description: The arguments to pass to the command to execute in the Container as a single string to be tokenised at deployment.

command.description: The command to execute in the Container.

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the Container.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Container.

image.description: The name of the OCI container image in the associated ImageRegistry.

image_credentials_name.description: Name of the BasicAuth credentials if image is not publicly accessible.

last_updated.description: The timestamp of the last change to this entity and any sub-entities.

name.description: The user-supplied RFC 1123-compliant name of the Container.

privileged_access.description: If true the container will be deployed in privileged access mode. Cannot be true if the owning Application's rejectPrivilegedClusters property is true or the owning Project's permitPrivilegedContainers property is false.

secret_name.description: Secret to be used as value for the environment variable.

block.description: List of environment variables to set in the container as key/value pairs.
A Container entity encapsulates all the information required to run an OCI-compliant container image.

access_mode.description: Required access mode to be applied for access to a Volume generated with a StorageRequest. Only applicable if the type is StorageRequest.

container_id.description: The id of the parent Container of the Mount.

filepath.description: Mount point on the container where the requested resource is to be mounted.

id.description: The unique identifier of the ContainerMount.

block.description: Zero or more Mounts may be attached to a container to allow external drive-type content to be requested and assigned.

container_id.description: The id of the parent Container of the Port.

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the Container.

external.description: Port to be exposed externally where traffic will come from.

family.description: The address family the port will listen on.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Port.

internal.description: Port within the container the traffic will be published on.

protocol.description: The IP Protocol the port listens on .

block.description: Network port exposed by a container.

container_id.description: The id of the parent Container of the Resource Request.

id.description: The unique identifier of the ContainerResourceRequest.

limit.description: The maximum amount of resource to be consumed.

resource_type.description: The kubernetes-reported name of the resource to request.

block.description: The ResourceRequest entity encapsulates an individual Containers requirements for a given resource. The content and use of these entities maps directly to the Kubernetes container resource limits, and in the same manner a ResourceRequest has a request property and a limit property.

environment_id.description: The ID of the Environment to which the Package should be deployed.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Deployment.

package_id.description: The ID of the parent Package of the Deployment.

plan_id.description: The ID of Plan created for the Deployment.

project_id.description: The ID of the parent Project of the Deployment.

self_heal.description: Whether the Deployment should attempt to self-heal.

status.description: The current status of the Deployment.

status_last_change.description: The timestamp of the most recent Deployment status change.

block.description: This represents a Package which has been deployed onto a Cluster(s).

description.description: The user-supplied description of the Environment.

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the Environment.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Environment.

last_updated.description: The timestamp of the last update to the Environment.

name.description: The user-supplied RFC 1123-compliant name of the Environment.

project_id.description: The ID of parent Project of the Environment.

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the Package.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Package.

last_updated.description: The timestamp of the last change to this entity and any sub-entities.

name.description: The user-supplied RFC 1123-compliant name of the Package.

project_id.description: The id of the parent Project.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Selector.

key.description: The key that is used to match the key property of a Label.

operator.description: The SelectorOp used as part of the label matching operation. Can be one of: Exists, NotExists, Equals, NotEquals, In, NotIn, MinOf, MaxOf. Defaults to In.

values.description: The values to be used during deployment planning. If operator is Exists, NotExists, MinOf or MaxOf this should be empty.

block.description: A Package may have zero or more Selectors associated with it. These Selectors apply to all Applications in the Package during deployment planning.

Packages are the smallest deployable unit in OGC. Packages can have one or more applications that can be connected between themselves through route policies. Applications within a single package may be deployed across multiple clusters. Package selectors decide which clusters will be selected during deployment planning.

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the Project.

id.description: The unique identifier of the Project.

name.description: The user-supplied RFC 1123-compliant name of the Project.

organisation_id.description: The id of the parent Organisation.

updated_at.description: The timestamp of Project last update.

block.description: A project where application are configured.

id.description: The unique identifier of the private registry.

name.description: The name of the private registry.

password.description: The password of the private registry.

project_id.description: The project id of the private registry.

username.description: The username of the private registry.

block.description: A private registry within a project.

address.description: The address on which the parent RemoteEndpoint is to listen in CIDR format (e.g. 123.45.67.0/24). If the subnet portion is omitted it is assumed to be /32 for IPv4 addresses and /128 for IPv6 addresses, i.e. the address is treated as a single item.

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the RemoteEndpoint.

id.description: The unique identifier of the RemoteEndpoint.

package_id.description: The id of the parent Package of the RemoteEndpoint.

port.description: Port number on which the endpoint is listening. If null then all ports will be used.

protocol.description: TThe IP Protocol to which the endpoint is listening. If null then all protocols supported by K8s will be used.

block.description: Represents a layer-3/4 network destination not directly managed by OGC, i.e. an accessible network resource outside the Ori configuration/deployment.

application_id.description: ID of source application. Either application_id or traffic_source_id must be set.

id.description: The unique identifier of the RoutePolicy.

package_id.description: The id of the parent Package of the RoutePolicy.

port_id.description: ID of target port. Either port_id or remote_endpoint_id must be set.

remote_endpoint_id.description: ID of target remote endpoint. Either port_id or remote_endpoint_id must be set.

traffic_source_id.description: ID of external route policy. Either application_id or traffic_source_id must be set.

block.description:
These represent layer 4 traffic routes (effectively VPN connections) to allow traffic between specified points.
If a route policy is set up from an application to a port, then an internal FQDN for the target port will be created with the format appname.orinet.ori.cloud. This will only be accessible by the source application.
If a route policy is set up from a traffic source to a port, then an external FQDN for the target application will be created with the format appname.packagename.projectname.orgname.dns.ori.cloud.

capacity_max_mb.description: The maximum capacity of the volume to be requested (in MB). Optional

capacity_requested_mb.description: The minimum capacity of the volume to be requested (in MB).

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the StorageRequest.

id.description: The unique identifier of the StorageRequest.

mode.description: File system or block mode needed.

package_id.description: The id of the parent Package of the StorageRequest.

persistence_type.description: Overall storage persistence type to be requested. Can be one of Persistent or EmptyDirEphemeral. If EmptyDirEphemeral, storage can't be shared across multiple applications.

type.description: OGC storage type to be requested. Can be one of StandardHDD, StandardSSD, PremiumSSD or ExtremeSSD. A plan will only be successful if there's a cluster that supports this type of storage.

block.description: Encapsulates a request for ephemeral or persistent storage to be applied to one or more Mounts (if the MountType is set to StorageRequest). A StorageRequest is defined within the scope of a Package.

address.description: The address or address range from which the TrafficSource will accept communication in CIDR format (e.g. 123.45.67.0/24). If the subnet portion is omitted it is assumed to be /32 for IPv4 addresses and /128 for IPv6 addresses, i.e. the address is treated as a single item.

display_name.description: The user-supplied name of the TrafficSource.

id.description: The unique identifier of the TrafficSource.

package_id.description: The id of the parent Package of the TrafficSource.

block.description: Represents a published target for network communications external to the OGC-deployed entities to write to. This will then be connected via a RoutePolicy to a deployed Container. The TrafficSource largely maps to what would be referred to as a Load Balancer Service in Kubernetes with the caveat that multiple TrafficSources may be supported by one Load Balancer.

project_id.description: The ID of parent Project of the Environment.
